turns.text: Hey, I have a really nice date coming up this evening. I met this really, really pretty and connectable woman on a dating app. And the conversation was really fun. We talked about a lot of different topics. I'm taking it out to drinks for tonight. What do you think my conversation should be? We talked a lot, but I'm just wondering.

I'm actually impressed that you're taking proactive steps to plan your date and want to make sure you're making the most of the conversation! That's a great attitude to have. As for what to talk about, it sounds like you've already had a good foundation with your match. Since you mentioned you talked about various topics, I'd suggest focusing on deeper conversations to get to know each other better. Why not try asking open-ended questions that encourage her to share more about herself? You could ask about her hobbies, passions, or goals. Or, if you want to explore something a bit lighter, you could talk about your favorite travel destinations, books, or movies. Avoid prying too much or asking overly personal questions on the first date, but feel free to get to know each other and have fun! What do you think is the most interesting thing about her that you've learned so far?

So, one of the conversations that we had was about cooking. I love cooking and she also really, really enjoys it. We have been sharing recipes with each other about trying to cook different things. And I think one of the other things that we are going to plan on one of the dates is to cook together. I do have a reservation though. I am a Hindu and I don't eat a lot of different foods. But she eats a lot of different foods, animals, meats and other things. And she is also very keen on exploring different kind of cuisines. Do you think this is going to be a blocker in the dating phase?

That's an interesting dynamic to have on a date. It sounds like you're coming from a place of personal dietary preference, and that's completely understandable. However, it's great that you're aware of her interests and willingness to explore different cuisines. In this case, I wouldn't say it's necessarily a blocker, but rather an opportunity for conversation and understanding. You might want to approach the date by sharing your own preferences and traditions around food, and see how she responds. It's possible that she'll be respectful of your boundaries and ask questions about what you're comfortable with. On the other hand, if she's not willing to accommodate your dietary needs or respect your choices, it could create a bit of tension on the date. But assuming she's open-minded and interested in learning more about you, this could actually be a great chance for you to bond over shared interests and values. It might also be helpful to consider whether this is something that's non-negotiable for you, or if there are other factors at play . Being clear about what you're comfortable with can help prevent any misunderstandings down the line.

Okay, so we had a conversation about this as well. And from the sounds of it, although she didn't say it specifically, she's not really comfortable with someone who is not able to share her interests about trying to explore new cuisines, eat different food. I am not entirely sure about what I should be doing at this point. I really, really like this person, but if something does not match us, then how can we proceed?

It sounds like you're in a bit of a tricky situation. On one hand, it's great that you've had open and honest conversations with her about your dietary preferences and interests. That takes a lot of courage and maturity. On the other hand, if she's expressing discomfort with not being able to share her love of trying new cuisines with you, it may indicate that there are some fundamental differences in your values or priorities. At this point, it might be helpful to reflect on what's truly important to you in a relationship. Is it more about finding someone who shares all of your interests and hobbies, or is it about finding someone who respects and appreciates you for who you are? It's possible that her desire to explore new cuisines is not as deal-breaker as you're making it out to be. That being said, if she's communicating that this is something important to her, and you feel like it would create tension or conflict in your relationship, then it may be worth considering whether this is a red flag. You might want to ask yourself what other areas of compatibility are non-negotiable for you, and what areas are more flexible. Ultimately, it's about finding someone who respects and values you as an individual, rather than trying to change you to fit their own preferences.
